locator.section: Dawn Collect and its conclusion, followed by the commemoration of St Anastasia and its own conclusion.

entries.claim: The Dawn Collect and the separate Oratio for St Anastasia appear in the Mass file. The proper calls for Per eundem and the commemoration for Per Dominum. Both conclusions and their responses come from the Mass Ordo.

locator.section: Postcommunio continuing Monday after the first Sunday of the Passion, above the Tuesday heading; Per Dominum nostrum through Deus.

entries.claim: This separate Postcommunion prints the accented conclusion with no comma after Christum and the colon and uppercase Qui after tuum, ending with Deus. The composite uses nostrum through Deus.; the cue words Per Dóminum come from p. 19, and this page supplies neither the final duration nor Amen.

locator.section: Top conclusion and response before the Nativity preface dialogue; Per omnia saecula saeculorum. R. Amen.

entries.claim: The top chant line prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen. The composite joins musical syllable divisions and omits the response marker. Only these five words are used; the Nativity preface dialogue and body are excluded.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a; Father-addressed oration conclusion

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion, ending with Amen. It controls the expansion rule, not the selected composite transcript's accents or its accidental seams.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 b; mention of the Son at the beginning of an oration

entries.claim: RG 115 b prescribes Per eundem Dominum nostrum, etc. ut supra when an oration addressed to the Father mentions the Son at its beginning. This Collect names the Son in its opening clause (nova incarnáti Verbi tui luce), and its printed cue instantiates the rule. The end-mention rule in 115 c is not used here.
